label: def:atomic-braid
title: Atomic braid $H_{A+Z}(q)$
html:
Definition. The atomic braid of a neutral atom (Z, N) is the element of H_{A+Z}(q) obtained by assembling Z protons, N neutrons, and Z electrons into a single Hecke algebra with A + Z strands, where A = Z + N. The crossing coefficients are:

See Table 1.

The ground-state ordering is determined by:

  1. Nuclear ordering: minimize \Phi_1 over all permutations of Z protons and N neutrons.
  2. Electron insertion: greedily insert each of Z electrons at the position minimizing \Phi_1.

Tractability of clause 1 (2026-08-25). As written, clause 1 quantifies over all \binom{A}{Z} distinct nucleon arrangements, so it is exponential in A and is not evaluable for most of the range the mass table covers: \binom{12}{6} = 924 for {}^{12}\mathrm{C} but \binom{40}{20} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{11} for {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca}. Clause 2 is already greedy and therefore polynomial; clause 1 is not, and the asymmetry between them is not explained here. No polynomial rule is substituted — that would be inventing mathematics the corpus has not derived — so the definition stands as stated, with the cost of taking it literally recorded. Any computation quoting a ground-state ordering for A \gtrsim 14 is therefore using some unstated restriction of clause 1 and should say which.

The greedy insertion produces ep pairs: each electron sits immediately before its proton. The \mathfrak{n}e = \mathrm{id} crossing means electrons pass through neutrons without generating Hecke generators.

The atomic braid carries the electron shell: the three electronic rows of Table 1 — \mathfrak{p}e, \mathfrak{n}e, ee — are part of the definition, not an optional dressing. It is therefore a different object from the electron-free nuclear core \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{3A}(q), which places three quark strands on each nucleon and carries no electron content (notation register). The two are not two conventions for one braid: H_{A+Z}(q) cannot contain a word on 3A strands at any A, since A + Z < 3A whenever Z \geq 1. The symbol \mathcal{A} denotes the atom defined here; an element of H_{3A}(q) is written \mathcal{B}_K.

For hydrogen (A = 1): the bare [e, \mathfrak{p}] braid is LP-unstable. The \mathfrak{p}e crossing uses the \mathcal{B}_3-dressed eigenvalues (q^5, -q^{-5}) instead of the bare (q^{-1}, -q).
